mainTopic: Resolving two conflicting ברייתות about eating קדשים when the מזבח or משכן is not standing
overview: The גמרא has been dealing with two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other. One says the meat of קרבנות may not be eaten at a certain time, and the other says it may be eaten 'in two locations.' The גמרא gives two different answers. First, the ברייתות follow two different opinions: רבי ישמעאל and the רבנן. Second, both ברייתות may be about קדשי קדשים, with no disagreement at all. In that second answer, 'two locations' is explained by timing, starting with the time before the לויים set up the משכן. The rest of that explanation continues right after these words.

steps.title: The two ברייתות follow two different opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the contradiction by assigning one ברייתא to רבי ישמעאל and the other to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל, and that ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction between the two ברייתות by saying they come from two different תנאים who disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא, which forbids eating, follows רבי ישמעאל. He learns the law of the meat of a בכור, which is from קדשים קלים, from the law of its blood, so the meat cannot be eaten when the מזבח is damaged or missing. The second ברייתא, which allows eating, follows the רבנן, who disagree with him. With this answer, the ברייתות are no longer a contradiction. They simply reflect a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: This one (pointing to one of the two sources)
The Sages, the majority view, who disagree with רבי ישמעאל

steps.confusionAlert: Saying 'this follows X, that follows Y' does not mean either ברייתא is wrong. It means each one is correct according to a different תנא.

phrases.english: This one follows Rabbi Yishmael; that one follows the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the ברייתא that forbids eating; 'that one' is the ברייתא that allows eating in two locations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between two ברייתות raised just before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the sources to different תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to give opposite rulings on the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are not contradictory. One reflects רבי ישמעאל's view, and the other reflects the רבנן's view.

steps.title: Both ברייתות are about the holiest קרבנות, and 'two locations' means a time before the משכן is set up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a second answer: both ברייתות speak about קדשי קדשים, and 'two locations' refers to the time before the לויים set up the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say this: both ברייתות are talking about קדשי קדשים. And what does 'in two locations' mean? Before the לויים set up the משכן…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to answer the contradiction, without needing a מחלוקת. It begins explaining the phrase 'two locations,' and that explanation continues right after these words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer, both ברייתות can agree with everyone, because both are about קדשי קדשים. The גמרא explains the phrase 'in two locations' by timing, connected to when the משכן was set up. The first situation is when the Jews arrived at a new camp but the לויים had not yet set up the משכן. The rest of the explanation continues right after these words.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)
The holiest קרבנות (the eaten ones are like חטאת and אשם)
In two locations (here explained as two situations)
The Levites, who took apart and set up the משכן

steps.confusionAlert: 'Two locations' sounds like two ordinary places. The גמרא instead explains it by timing, starting with the time before the לויים set up the משכן.

phrases.english: Both this and that are about offerings of the most sacred order;
and what does 'in two locations' mean?
before the Levites erect the Tabernacle,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא וְהָא בְּקׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the same contradiction answered in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case and wording of the ברייתא (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות seemed to disagree, so they needed to be split between two תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both ברייתות deal with קדשי קדשים, and 'two locations' is explained by timing, beginning with the time before the לויים set up the משכן. So there is no need for a מחלוקת.
